To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clonal deletion occurs in the thymi of HYcd4 transgenic male mice and that the deletion event is mediated by cortical dendritic cells.

cortical dendritic cells are the major antigen-presenting cells that induce thymocyte deletion in the HYcd4 system, and that cortical dendritic and thymic epithelial cells are not major antigen-presenting or apoptotic cells in the HYcd system.

thymic cortical epithelial cells are unable to promote negative selection of HYcd4 thymocytes, and that rare CD11c + dendritic cells in the thymus are required for negative selection of HYCD4 thymocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cortical dendritic cells in the deletion process, which has been largely overlooked to date.
how thymocytes are deleted in the cortex and how this is regulated by the thymic microenvironment.
the mechanisms of thymic negative selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cortical dendritic cells are the major APC involved in negative selection, although cortical epithelial cells can also promote deletion.
cortical dendritic cells promote negative selection of self-reactive thymiocytes in the HYcd4 system.
cortical thymocytes can be eliminated by negative selection, but the process is not as efficient as in the medulla, and the cortical environment is not optimal for negative selection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thymic medullary environment is not necessary for negative selection, but that cortical dendritic cells play a key role.
clonal deletion can occur in the thymus in the absence of medullary epithelial cells, but the efficiency of this deletion is enhanced by dendritic cells.
the cortical environment is permissive for negative selection, but that dendritic cells are the major antigen-presenting cells driving clonal deletion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thymic microenvironment does not have to be specialized to promote negative selection.
cortical epithelial cells and radioresistant antigen presenting cells do not efficiently promote negative selection.
clonal deletion can occur in the cortical microenvironment, but the efficiency of this deletion process requires the presence of cortical dendritic cells.
